name: Mince and rice stuffed peppers
summary: Red and yellow pepper halves filled with lean beef mince, brown rice, tomato and grated baby marrow, baked soft under a light sprinkle of cheese.
about: Stuffed peppers are cooked across the Mediterranean, the Balkans and the Middle East, usually with a filling of rice and minced meat. Baking the halves open-faced keeps them quick to fill, the grated baby marrow disappears into the mince, and each person gets two colourful halves on the plate.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C if your oven is a fan oven). Put the rice in a saucepan of boiling salted water and boil for 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well.

While the rice cooks, halve the peppers lengthways through the stalk and pull out the seeds and white ribs, leaving the stalk on so the halves hold their shape. Lay them cut side up in a roasting dish, rub with 1 tsp of the oil and roast for 15 minutes, until they just start to soften.
Heat the rest of the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, paprika and oregano and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.

Turn the heat up to medium-high, add the mince and break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook for about 8 minutes, until browned with no pink left and the juices have cooked away. Stir in the baby marrow and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, salt and pepper and simmer on low for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick rather than runny. Stir in the drained rice and taste for salt.
Spoon the filling into the pepper halves, pressing it down and piling it up, and put any extra around them in the dish. Scatter over the cheddar.

Bake for 20 minutes, until the peppers are tender when you push in the tip of a knife and the cheese has melted and turned golden at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes and serve two halves each with a green salad.
prepNote: Fill the roasted peppers up to a day ahead and chill; bake for 30 minutes from the fridge.
